rows.65:0fa4:
For a start, I opened a file close at hand.
Let's see...
"I got a perm, even though I was told it was against the rules.
But now I hear the student council has a campaign going to lift the ban on perms.
If that passes, I'll be left wondering what I was even sorry for.
Anyway, I apologize."
There's no rule banning perms now.
I wonder if it was dropped before this person graduated?{p}
rows.65:13bc:
He was the honor-student type, the kind of guy who'd never once been scolded by a teacher.
He was calm, he served as class rep, and everyone said he was so earnest.
He was pretty popular with girls, apparently, but he didn't have a girlfriend.
Ever since he was little, he'd been told what a good boy he was.
Though he himself didn't seem to think so.
Well, I bet lots of people have felt that way.{p}When the people around you just decide on their own what kind of person you are.
rows.65:1cac:
Kawahara had a bad feeling, and when he started to open the textbook, he could feel something tucked inside.
No way.
That's what Kawahara thought.
Could Koizumi have stolen the question sheet and slipped it into this textbook...?
No, there's no way.
A coincidence like that just couldn't happen.
And I can't think of anything I did to make him hate me that much.
But if the question sheet really is tucked in this textbook...
Kawahara started to feel sick.
He could feel his face getting hot.
His heart seemed to be beating faster and faster, too.
Come to think of it, Koizumi's grades were supposed to be pretty good.
But after every big test, the one who came out on top was always Kawahara.
Was that why Koizumi resented him?
Kawahara imagined all sorts of things.
If he opened the textbook, he'd know what was tucked inside, but if it was the question sheet, he might be the one under suspicion.
With that thought, he couldn't bring himself to open the textbook.{p}
rows.65:2384:
"Oh, the textbook?
I'm pretty sure I gave it back."
That was his simple answer.
The guy he'd lent the textbook to surely had nothing to do with Koizumi's suspicious behavior.
Still, if this guy had only given the textbook back sooner...
For an instant, Kawahara glared at him.
What a sloppy guy he is.
Was I an idiot for lending my textbook to a guy like this?
No, he's the idiot.
He never thinks about the trouble he causes other people.
I'd love to just punch him.
Pound him till his nose bleeds, then kick him right in the gut...{p}
rows.65:2664:
His heart was way more twisted than any ordinary student's.
A backlash, I guess you'd call it.
Apparently it's always the people who hold themselves in check who have it worst.
Kawahara's heart was full of hatred for the guy.
If there really was a question sheet stuck in that textbook, why not sneak it into this guy's desk?
And then go rat him out to the teacher...{p}
rows.65:2a88:
At the next break, Kawahara went up to the roof.
After making sure nobody was around, he started to open the textbook he'd hidden under his uniform.
It was really windy that day.
To keep whatever was inside the textbook from blowing away, he moved into a corner, out of the wind.
He was just nervously trying to peek inside, when...
The door to the roof slowly opened, and he saw someone's shadow.
That silhouette wasn't a student's.
From the necktie flapping in the wind, he knew right away it was a teacher.
The teacher was far off, but seemed to be watching Kawahara closely.
You see, someone had told on him for acting strange.
So the teacher had followed him up there.
The teacher came closer, one step at a time.
The teacher's mouth was clearly about to say something.
And the teacher's eyes were fixed on the textbook in Kawahara's hands.
With every step closer, the shadow grew bigger.
rows.65:31c8:
My guess is that Hashimoto, the one who wrote this apology letter saying, 'It's my fault Kawahara died'... offered to return it for him, and tucked the love letter inside.
The reason Koizumi was messing with Kawahara's textbook was to look at that love letter.
I don't know why he did it.
Maybe he saw Hashimoto slip the letter in and got curious, or maybe there was some other reason.
I think Kawahara's death was his own fault.
That's what he gets for thinking all those needless things.{p}
rows.65:37dc:
Then darkness spread out before my eyes.
Here and there in the darkness, I could see glimmers of light.{p}
rows.65:3d9c:
I'm kind of tired.
Maybe I'll take a little nap.
..............................Ah!
This is no time for that.
I have to do this interview properly.
The seventh person hasn't even shown up, and if I miss this story too, we'll be down to five wonders.
I don't want Hino yelling at me.
Um, let me try reading one of these files lying around.{p}
rows.65:4440:
He ran.
Why wouldn't anyone believe him?
Could it be they knew how he was always cursing everyone in his head?
That's what he was thinking as he ran.
He just got more and more frantic.
rows.65:4cc8:
And the last thing he wrote... should be in that file there.
{b}, let me see that a sec.
See, it's filed down near the bottom.
"...Why won't anybody believe a word I say?
I cannot trust the teacher.
Nor can I trust myself, for agonizing over something like this."
They say Kawahara killed himself after writing this.{p}
